title: Agent Constitution
description: Structural schema for a digest-pinned agent constitution. This validates SHAPE only. It cannot validate that your values are the right values, that your rules are genuinely non-negotiable, or that your authority order is correct -- those need a human, which is what the change-control process is for. See prompts/G01-constitution-preamble.md.

constitution_id.description: Stable identifier, verified in code. Prevents a different valid constitution being swapped in wholesale.

purpose.description: What the agent is for and, explicitly, what it must not replace.

function.description: What this value OBLIGES, in behavioral terms. A value with no stated obligation is decoration.

values_scope.description: Required in spirit if your values derive from a particular tradition.

authority_order.description: Highest first. The agent itself goes last. This is the field that decides conflicts between legitimate inputs.

non_negotiable_rules.description: Only rules you would ship a broken build rather than weaken. Two are load-bearing in every domain and cannot be checked by this schema: an anti-override rule enumerating its channels, and an escalation rule naming a human destination. Check those in code -- see reference/constitution.py's REQUIRED_RULE_KEYWORDS.

clarifications.description: Scope narrowing that creates no new permission. Each entry should state which rule it clarifies.

required_change_control.description: The steps a substantive change must pass. Include re-pinning the digest in the SAME commit -- a lone re-pin commit is the shape of an unreviewed governance change.
